recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No FHIR-45008 follow-up is needed unless the work group later chooses a broader BodyStructure editorial cleanup unrelated to this approved clarification.
issue_request: FHIR-45008 was Applied with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for R6. The OO work group requested that BodyStructure.includedStructure.bodyLandmarkOrientation mention a body landmark such as a navel, scar, or implanted device, and that BodyStructure/skin-patch be expanded with a landmark example such as 2 cm distal from a heart tattoo.
initial_application: The Jira comment says the change was added to the build in HL7/fhir PR #3101, citing commit 8909642886c3490e04706499e7304f91e12038d6. Source history shows the substantive implementation in 238839faadab4fc3f5b32733442ec222ff33897d, which updated source/bodystructure/structuredefinition-BodyStructure.xml and source/bodystructure/bodystructure-example-skin-patch.xml before PR #3101 was merged as 0064cbe1d23c1030df096f3c91c1cf214535bda6.
additional_context: The linked Zulip thread records the motivating question about endotracheal tubes, stents, prostheses, and other artificial artifacts, and Rob Hausam confirmed that artificial landmarks are consistent with bodyLandmarkOrientation intent when they provide a relatively fixed reference point. OO minutes for 2024-03-22 recorded the same FHIR-45008 block-vote disposition. BodyStructure is active in source/fhir.ini, and later BodyStructure source history did not remove the requested definition or example.
reconciliation: No source edit was needed. The active StructureDefinition already includes implanted device in the bodyLandmarkOrientation definition, and the active skin-patch example already includes bodyLandmarkOrientation with a heart tattoo, 2.0 cm distance, and distal surface orientation.
